The PKGBUILD contains only standard top-level variable and array assignments (pkgname, pkgver, source URLs, checksums, depends, etc.). The package_*() functions are not executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Checksums are provided rather than SKIP. This is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practice and poses no supply-chain risk at the parse/sourcing stage.
</details>

<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    The PKGBUILD defines three packages (vst3-bin, lv2-bin, standalone-bin) and a metapackage that depends on all of them. Source files are downloaded from the official ZL-Audio/ZLEqualizer GitHub releases (zip URLs) and the license from a raw GitHub URL, both pointing to the upstream project. SHA‑256 sums for x86_64, aarch64, and the license are supplied. No `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or other code-execution constructs appear. The `source` fields reference the upstream tag `refs/tags/1.4.2`, i.e., a pinned commit rather than a mutable branch. Although the file lists `makepkg`-related options, there is no explicit `build()` step invoking `make`, `cmake`, or other compilers; the usual AUR workflow is implied. Installations target standard library directories (`usr/lib/vst3`, `usr/lib/lv2`, `usr/bin/zlequalizer`) and place licenses under `usr/share/licenses/...`. This aligns with routine AUR packaging and shows no attempts to exfiltrate data, inject code, or modify system caches outside the package scope.
  </details>

  <summary>PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging, no malicious activity detected.</summary>
